facts.subject: Pickpocketing
facts.value: stunned 9 ticks (cannot pickpocket for 8); NPC may be pickpocketed every 2 ticks
facts.statement: A failed pickpocket damages and stuns the player (9 ticks movement, 8 ticks no pickpocketing); eating while stunned adds the food delay. Successful pickpockets can be repeated every 2 ticks.

sources.title: Thieving
sources.quote: NPCs may be pickpocketed every two ticks (1.2 seconds).

sources.title: Thieving
sources.quote: Being stunned prevents the player from moving for nine ticks (5.4 seconds), and from further pickpocketing for eight ticks (4.8s).

sources.title: Stun (status)
sources.quote: When a player fails to [[pickpocket]] a target, they are temporarily stunned as well as take damage, scaling depending on the [[Thieving#Thievable_NPCs|thievable NPC]]. The player will be prevented from moving and attempting further pickpockets for several ticks. Wearing a [[Dodgy necklace]] gives the player a 25% chance to avoid being stunned upon failure. This stacks multiplicatively with the [[Shadow Veil]] spell, where Shadow Veil will attempt to avoid the stun first for a total of 36.25% chance to avoid the stun.

sources.title: Master Farmer
sources.quote: ''' Master Farmers''' are adept farmers that can be [[pickpocketed]] to receive a variety of [[seeds]]. Level 38 [[Thieving]] is required to pickpocket them. Successful pickpockets can result in most types of seeds, excluding [[tree seed]]s and [[fruit tree seed]]s. 43 Thieving experience is granted upon successfully pickpocketing a Master Farmer. Failing to pickpocket a Master Farmer results in being [[stun (status)|stunned]] for five seconds and taking three hitpoints of damage. If the player's inventory is full, they will be unable to pickpocket them.

facts.caveat: Exact tick counts (9 stun, 8 no-pickpocket, 2-tick cadence) appear only on the Thieving page; the Stun (status) page confirms the mechanic qualitatively. The Master Farmer page says "stunned for five seconds" and the Thieving other-activities table lists 4.8 s: the same 8 ticks rounded differently. Per-NPC stun damage varies (1-6) and is in the Thieving NPC table.

sources.title: Stealing valuables
sources.quote: To steal valuables, players must first acquire house keys. The fastest way to acquire them is through pickpocketing wealthy citizens in the [[bazaar]], where they are received at a rate of around 1/17. Another way to obtain house keys is by [[big fishing net|big net]] [[Fishing]] at the [[Fishing spot (Civitas illa Fortis)|fishing spot]] in the park in east Fortis, at a rate of 1/10.

sources.title: Stealing valuables
sources.quote: At random, a flashing arrow [[File:Yellow arrow map marker.png|link=]] will appear above one of the objects in the house and {{mes|You notice something shine somewhere else in the house.|colour=#a53fff}} appears in the chatbox. Searching these objects will net a one-time bonus of 14 valuables and 630 Thieving experience. The arrow will disappear after around 7 seconds if the player has not stolen from it before then. It is recommended to loot the object in the middle of the house to reduce the risk of missing the shiny object.

sources.title: Stealing valuables
sources.quote: The homeowner will return 180–190 seconds after they left the house;  a whistle serves as an audio cue to warn the player, and a game message in the chatbox will state {{mes|You hear someone outside spot the homeowner coming back!|colour=#ff289d}} At this point, the player should prepare to exit from the open window. The player is able to continue burgling for a short while after this message, until the homeowner opens their door. sources.title: Master Farmer
sources.quote: ''' Master Farmers''' are adept farmers that can be [[pickpocketed]] to receive a variety of [[seeds]]. Level 38 [[Thieving]] is required to pickpocket them. facts.subject: Pyramid Plunder
facts.statement: Pyramid Plunder gives about 125,000 XP/h at 71-80, 190,000 at 81-90 and 270,000 at 91+ assuming soloing with a pharaoh's sceptre teleport; about 335 games take you from 91 to 99; the wiki page gives 120,000 at 71 and over 275,000 at 91+ in the best case.

sources.title: Thieving training
sources.quote: It takes approximately 335 games to get from 91 to 99 in Pyramid Plunder.

sources.title: Pyramid Plunder
sources.quote: In the most optimal scenario, up to 120,000 [[Thieving]] experience can be gained per hour at level 71, and upwards of 275,000 experience at level 91, accounting for failed searches and the occasional resupply. Rates are also dependent on the player's equipment, e.g. a [[Pharaoh's sceptre]] will nullify the time spent entering the pyramid.

facts.caveat: Wiki conflict: Thieving training table says 125,000 (71-80), 190,000 (81-90), 270,000 (91+); the Pyramid Plunder page says up to 120,000 at level 71 and upwards of 275,000 at level 91 (best case). Conservative: 120,000 / 270,000. Wiki estimate, not a guaranteed rate: it assumes the stated supplies, good practice and the stated unlocks; expect lower rates while learning.

facts.subject: Pyramid Plunder
facts.value: Saradomin brews, stamina potions, antipoison (or serpentine helm); pharaoh's sceptre recharged with noted golden artefacts; sceptre drops from golden chests
facts.statement: Bring high-healing food (Saradomin brews), stamina potions and antipoison (araxyte venom sac or serpentine helm for poison immunity). A charged pharaoh's sceptre teleports to Jalsavrah; recharge with noted artefacts; desert diary raises charge cap. The sceptre is only found in Pyramid Plunder and can be sold. GE items: "Pharaoh's sceptre", "Saradomin brew(4)", "Stamina potion(4)".

facts.subject: Rogues' Castle chests
facts.value: 84 Thieving; Wilderness levels 52-56 (chests at ~54); 3 chests, 20.4 s respawn; Search for traps first
facts.statement: Rogues' Castle chests need 84 Thieving, give 701.7 XP and respawn in 20.4 s (three chests). The castle is in the deep Wilderness (levels 52-56, chests at about 54). You must Search for traps before opening, and the rogues (level 135, max hit 15, Protect from Melee blocks) attack when a chest is looted. The Chaos Elemental may wander to the entrance.

sources.title: Chest (Rogues' Castle)
sources.quote: Player-killers are extremely common at the rogue's castle, and frequently [[world hop]] looking for victims, often in the courtyard itself or the shed just east of the chests. To try to keep the valuable loot, it's recommended for players to use a non-deadly [[:Category:Self-damaging items|self-damaging item]] such as a [[dwarven rock cake]] or [[locator orb]] to continuously keep their hitpoints as low as possible. Immediately on spotting a player-killer, the player should then use an [[Araxyte venom sac]], which deals 4 damage and will kill the player if they've kept their hitpoints below th

facts.caveat: Deep Wilderness (levels 52-56): player killers are "extremely common"; level 135 rogues (max hit 15, blocked by Protect from Melee) attack when a chest is looted; the Chaos Elemental (hits up to 28, ignores protection prayers) may wander to the entrance. The chest page warns a PvM death can still count as PvP if a player lands any hit, so the training-page "die to the rogues for a gravestone" tactic is not guaranteed. A death here would be run-ending on Hardcore Worlds. Chest XP is 701.7 per chest.
